title: The Castle That Served Supper
continuity: Episode 1 ends during chapter 1 preparations, before the first departure. This sequel begins at the inn after a brief recap of chapter 2 travel and ends at the chapter 3 departure.

selection.chapters1to8: 1 identity/equipment; 2–3 first sally, inn and knighting; 4 failed interventions with Andres and merchants; 5 neighbour brings him home; 6 scrutiny of books; 7 burning/walled library and Sancho recruited; 8 windmills, friars and unresolved Biscayan duel.
selection.chosen: 2–3 offer one complete evening with clear escalation. Going straight to windmills would omit the first sally and how he obtains his imagined authority.
selection.nextSuggested: Chapters 4–5: the rescue that makes things worse, followed by the merchants and return home. Later 6–7 can bridge to Sancho; chapter 8 is its own action episode, ending at Cervantes’s cliffhanger unless chapter 9 is authorized.

storyCircle.you: Returning student helper remembers a funny hopeful man.
storyCircle.need: Help him settle in and get through the night without trouble.
storyCircle.go: One written question opens the journal into the inn.
storyCircle.search: Manage supper, ribbons, the request and supplies.
storyCircle.find: The host agrees to grant the ceremony; the goal seems attainable.
storyCircle.take: Heroic interpretation leads to real injuries and stones.
storyCircle.return: A hasty ceremony gets Quixote away; journal takes student home.
storyCircle.change: Student distinguishes sincere intent and ceremonial success from actual care for neighbours.

characterCausality.Quixote: Wants to help and earn honour; treats chivalric books as practical authority; reads ordinary actions as heroic ritual or insult; attacks and feels confirmed by knighting.
characterCausality.Innkeeper: Initially enjoys a joke and wants manageable guests; plays along; injuries change his immediate motive to ending the danger; improvises ceremony.
characterCausality.Carriers: Need to water working animals; interpret armour as an obstruction; move it; suffer consequences unrelated to any wish to duel.
characterCausality.student: Initially assumes practical assistance and explanations can smooth things over; warnings fail; chooses small useful care and returns with a changed understanding.

choices: Six binary choices; 64 routes. All preserve source events. Variables only change later reflection, never grades or source outcomes. No chance command.
duration: Roughly 10–12 minutes plus four questions; an estimate to confirm in class.
vocabulary: Intertextuality, revision and close reading explicitly; adaptation in framing/sources. Do not force all six terms into the emotional ending.

art.prompt: Create a 16:9 visual-novel background of a modest roadside inn courtyard in La Mancha Spain around 1600, at night under a bright moon. No people or text. Match simple manga-inspired vector characters: clean dark slate outlines, flat muted colours, restrained two-tone cel shadows, simplified geometric scenery, no photorealistic surfaces or painterly texture. Eye-level camera, broad clear central foreground for standing characters. Low whitewashed inn with weathered clay roof, warm lantern at doorway on left, stable doorway at far right, stone well with a long low animal watering trough behind the standing area. Moonlit blue-grey paving, warm amber windows, plausible simple rural architecture, no castle towers. Keep background less contrasted than actors. Whole scene readable on a phone, welcoming at first but capable of tense night action.

publication: Separate unassigned teacher draft. Existing chapter-1 episode, published versions and class assignments unchanged.
